title: Session 8: Writing Workshop: From First Draft to Final Draft
summary: Apply everything: build an academic paragraph, check it with the sentence checklist and correction codes, write a second draft in the session, and finish with a final draft that uses every conjunction type and all four sentence structures correctly.

blocks.title: By the end of this session you can …
items: Plan and write an academic paragraph (topic sentence, support, conclusion)
Use the correction codes to find and fix your own mistakes
Rewrite a first draft into a second and final draft
Use all four conjunction types and all four sentence structures accurately

rows: states the main idea of the paragraph
simple or complex — clear and direct
gives a reason and explains it
Furthermore, / In addition, + compound or compound-complex
shows the other side, then answers it
Therefore, / As a result, + simple or complex

blocks.title: Model: Should students learn to cook at school?
blocks.task: Write one academic paragraph (120–150 words) giving your opinion.
text: Every student should learn to cook at school **(S — topic sentence)**. Because many teenagers rely on fast food, they often eat meals that are high in fat and sugar **(CX)**. Cooking lessons would teach them how to prepare simple, healthy dishes, and they would eat better at home **(C)**. Furthermore, cooking is a life skill; students who can cook will save money when they live alone **(CC: IC; IC with relative clause + DC)**. On the other hand, some people argue that schools do not have enough time for extra subjects **(CX — noun clause)**. However, a single lesson every two weeks would be enough, and it would not replace any important subject **(C)**. Not only would cooking improve students' health, but it would also make them more independent **(C — correlative)**. Therefore, cooking deserves a place in every school timetable **(S — concluding sentence)**.
notes: **All four structures** are used, and simple sentences are kept for the topic and concluding sentences (clear and strong).
**All four conjunction types:** FANBOYS (and), subordinating (because, when, that), correlative (not only … but also), conjunctive adverbs (Furthermore, However, Therefore, On the other hand).
**Punctuation:** DC, IC with a comma · IC; IC with a semicolon · comma + FANBOYS between ICs · comma after every sentence starter.
**Varied openings:** Every, Because, Cooking, Furthermore, On the other hand, However, Not only, Therefore.
**Counter-point and reply** make the argument balanced and academic.

rows: join it to an IC or add a subject/verb
full stop, comma + FANBOYS, semicolon, or make one clause dependent
same fixes as RO; never comma + however
check the comma rules: IC, FANBOYS IC · DC, IC · IC DC · IC; however, IC
check the meaning: contrast, result, reason, addition …
remove one: although … but / because … so
change the structure or the opening of the sentence
both … and = plural · either/neither … or/nor = nearer subject

items: ☐ My paragraph has a topic sentence, at least two supported points and a concluding sentence.
☐ I used **all four sentence structures** (S, C, CX, CC).
☐ I used **all four conjunction types** (FANBOYS, subordinating, correlative, conjunctive adverb).
☐ Every comma before FANBOYS has an IC on **both** sides.
☐ Every sentence that starts with a DC has a comma after the DC.
☐ Every however / therefore / moreover between two ICs has a **semicolon before** and a **comma after**.
☐ No fragments, no run-ons, no comma splices.
☐ No although … but and no because … so.
☐ My sentences start in different ways.
Your teacher returns your first draft (Session 7 homework) with correction codes.
Find each code and fix the mistake yourself — do not just copy the correct answer.
Use the checklist. Add any sentence structure or conjunction type that is missing.
Write the **second draft** in the session. Your teacher checks it live.
At home: write the **final draft** (homework) and submit it with the first and second drafts.

items.q: Label the structure: Although many students dislike homework, it helps them remember what they learn.
Add a counter-point sentence to a paragraph about uniforms, starting with On the other hand,
items.a: e.g. On the other hand, some students feel that uniforms stop them from expressing their personality.

items.q: Correct and give the code: Uniforms save time, students don't have to choose clothes.
items.a: **CS** → Uniforms save time because students don't have to choose clothes.

items.q: Correct and give the code: Although uniforms are expensive, but they last a long time.
items.a: **2L** → Although uniforms are expensive, they last a long time.

items.q: Write a concluding sentence with Therefore, for the topic "learning a second language".
items.a: e.g. Therefore, every student should learn at least one second language.

blocks.title: Session 8 Practice Quiz
blocks.intro: 15 questions. Choose the best answer. You see your score and the explanations at the end.

questions.q: Which sentence is the best **topic sentence**?
c: And it is useful, so many people learn it.
Learning a second language opens many doors for young people.

questions.q: Which code means two ICs joined with only a comma?
Although it is expensive, but it is worth it. Which code?
Not only would cooking improve health, but it would also save money. This uses …

c: Cooking is useful, and it is fun.
Because cooking saves money, it is useful, and many students enjoy it.
Cooking is useful because it saves money.
Students who can cook save money.
Students, who can cook save money.
Students who can cook, save money.
Students who, can cook save money.
questions.e: The relative clause is needed information → no commas.

questions.q: Neither the students nor the teacher ___ ready.
Which sentence has a correct comma?
c: Many people buy fast food, because it is cheap.
Many people, buy fast food because it is cheap.
Because fast food is cheap many people buy it.
Because fast food is cheap, many people buy it.

questions.q: Which shows the best **variety** of openings?
c: I think … I believe … I feel …

questions.q: Which fixes the run-on Homework is useful it helps us revise?
c: Homework is useful however it helps us revise.
Homework is useful, however, it helps us revise.
Homework is useful because it helps us revise.
Homework is useful, it helps us revise.

questions.q: What should a supporting point include?
c: a reason plus an explanation or example

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a second draft?
c: to make the paragraph shorter only
to fix the marked mistakes and improve structure and variety
to copy the first draft neatly
